C0006.title: Unfair Competition Case on Operating a Manual Traffic Platform to Disrupt Search Engine Algorithms
C0006.summary: A typical Beijing Intellectual Property Court case showed that Baidu v. Woai concerned the operation of a manual traffic platform that interfered with search engine algorithms. The court's reasoning treated organized non-genuine user feedback that affects search ranking and display opportunities, harms search-service evaluation systems, and disrupts normal business order as conduct that can constitute unfair competition. The case also highlights the need for search, recommendation, and advertising systems to detect non-genuine clicks, visits, and evaluation signals.
